title: No Free Swap: Protocol-Dependent Layer Redundancy in Transformers
authors: Gabriel Garcia
abstract: Replacement and interchange are different output-grounded notions of layer equivalence; their gap grows over Pythia training.
method: Replacement/interchange swap-KL; removal validation; controlled training
intervention_type: Weight replacement; layer interchange; deletion; averaging
main_claim: Training duration produces a protocol-dependent and pair-heterogeneous layer-equivalence gap.
relation_to_candidate_a: Directly overlaps training-time Pythia layer equivalence and intervention-family dependence; lacks Candidate A's independent-run top-1 and prospective damage matching.

title: The Remarkable Robustness of LLMs: Stages of Inference?
authors: Vedang Lad; Jin Hwa Lee; Wes Gurnee; Max Tegmark
abstract: LLMs retain much of their top-1 behavior under adjacent layer deletion and swapping, with depth-localized sensitivity.
primary_metric: Relative top-1 accuracy; KL; loss; entropy; task scores
main_claim: Middle layers are robust to structural intervention and depth exhibits staged sensitivity.
relation_to_candidate_a: Exact static anchor for Candidate A's block intervention and top-1 agreement statistic; no checkpoint trajectory or independent runs.

title: SteerCheck: Attribution Specificity and Alignment Leakage in Activation-Steering Audits
authors: Daming Luo; Christy Liang; Junyu Xuan
abstract: A preregistered activation-steering audit matches off-target KL and shows that comparator geometry still changes behavioral effects.
intervention_type: Activation steering directions and structured nulls
primary_metric: Off-target KL; behavioral effect; cosine; transfer
main_claim: KL matching does not make intervention directions exchangeable and family/alignment structure remains.
relation_to_candidate_a: Strong methodological collision with functional-budget matching and residual family structure, but not a pretraining/block-bypass study.

title: Divergent Token Metrics: Measuring Degradation to Prune Away LLM Components--and Optimize Quantization
authors: Bjorn Deiseroth; Max Meuer; Nikolas Gritsch; Constantin Eichenberg; Patrick Schramowski; Matthias Assenmacher; Kristian Kersting
abstract: Token-divergence metrics compare a compressed model with its base model and expose damage missed by aggregate metrics.
method: Reference-model divergent-token metrics for pruning and quantization
main_claim: Top-1 token disagreement is useful for component-level compression assessment.
relation_to_candidate_a: Candidate S is the complement of token disagreement on fixed contexts; metric novelty is absent even though Delta S across training is different.

title: Training Dynamics Impact Post-Training Quantization Robustness
authors: Albert Catalan-Tatjer; Niccolo Ajroldi; Jonas Geiping
abstract: Quantization degradation across hundreds of checkpoints is shaped strongly by learning-rate dynamics and can diverge from full-precision validation loss.
model_family: OLMo; SmolLM3; Apertus; OpenSci; Amber; Pythia-style controlled models
intervention_type: Post-training quantization; LR and averaging interventions
main_claim: Training dynamics, especially decay, govern robustness to quantization more than token count alone.
relation_to_candidate_a: Shows training-time perturbation robustness is already a substantial literature theme; perturbation and endpoint differ.

title: When Probing Accuracy Saturates, Fragility Resolves: A Complementary Metric for LLM Pre-Training Analysis
authors: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
abstract: Activation-noise fragility reveals representational changes across checkpoints after probe accuracy saturates, with an activation-scale confound explicitly corrected.
method: Activation-noise thresholding over checkpoints and probes
main_claim: Representational fragility continues to evolve during pretraining and raw cross-layer noise is scale-confounded.
relation_to_candidate_a: Overlaps training-time activation-noise fragility and confound control; does not test block bypass, top-1 output substitutability, or independent pretraining runs.

title: Not the Dimension, the Norm: What Matters in Gradient-Free Weight Perturbation of Language Models
authors: Taeyeong Kim; Ahhyun Kim; TaeHyeon Kim; Unggi Lee
abstract: Controlled gradient-free adaptation finds performance insensitive to subspace dimension and basis after scale correction, with perturbation norm defining a safe window.
main_claim: Norm is the live control in its gradient-free adaptation regime, while placement is not inert.
relation_to_candidate_a: A recent counterpoint to Candidate A's bounded raw-magnitude insufficiency; different intervention objective and no checkpoint trajectory.

title: Understanding Robustness of Transformers for Image Classification
authors: Srinadh Bhojanapalli; Ayan Chakrabarti; Daniel Glasner; Daliang Li; Thomas Unterthiner; Andreas Veit
abstract: ViTs are robust to multiple input and model perturbations and to removal of most individual layers, with robustness depending on pretraining data.
intervention_type: Layer removal; parameter and input perturbations
main_claim: Transformer layer-removal robustness and training data are linked in vision.
relation_to_candidate_a: Older cross-domain precursor to training/data-dependent layer-removal robustness; no LM trajectory or functional matching.

title: Efficient Parametric Approximations of Neural Network Function Space Distance
authors: Nikita Dhawan; Sicong Huang; Juhan Bae; Roger Baker Grosse
abstract: Function-space distance measures average output discrepancy and can be approximated compactly for downstream uses.
method: LAFTR parametric approximation to output discrepancy
corpus_data: Training sets in continual-learning and influence experiments
main_claim: Functional rather than raw parameter distance is an established object with practical utility.
relation_to_candidate_a: Undercuts any broad novelty claim for function-space over parameter-space measurement; no layer intervention or language-model trajectory.

title: Walking Noise: On Layer-Specific Robustness of Neural Architectures against Noisy Computations and Associated Characteristic Learning Dynamics
authors: Hendrik Borras; Bernhard Klein; Holger Froning
abstract: Layer-specific additive and multiplicative noise reveals heterogeneous robustness and characteristic adaptation during noisy training.
method: Layer-wise activation/weight noise and midpoint-noise fitting
corpus_data: MNIST; FashionMNIST; SVHN; CIFAR-10; Speech Commands
main_claim: Noise family and layer location change robustness; noise training changes the response.
relation_to_candidate_a: Closest early activation-noise robustness antecedent; not pretrained LMs or checkpoint-wise block substitutability.

title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models
authors: Cody Rushing; Neel Nanda
abstract: Ablated attention heads induce imperfect and prompt-variable self-repair across language-model families, partly through LayerNorm and anti-erasure neurons.
main_claim: Component damage is compensated nonuniformly and mechanism depends on architecture and prompt.
relation_to_candidate_a: Important mechanistic-intervention background; not a checkpoint trajectory or damage-matched family comparison.

title: ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models Are More Redundant Than You Expect
authors: Xin Men; Mingyu Xu; Qingyu Zhang; Qianhao Yuan; Bingning Wang; Hongyu Lin; Yaojie Lu; Xianpei Han; Weipeng Chen
abstract: Block Influence ranks low-impact layers for removal and enables training-free depth pruning.
method: Input-output cosine Block Influence and layer pruning
main_claim: Many final-model layers are redundant enough to prune.
relation_to_candidate_a: Static redundancy/pruning context; no pretraining trajectory, independent runs, or damage matching.

title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers
authors: Andrey Gromov; Kushal Tirumala; Hassan Shapourian; Paulo Glorioso; Daniel A. Roberts
abstract: Many deeper layers can be removed and cheaply healed while preserving benchmark performance.
main_claim: Substantial depth redundancy exists in final pretrained LMs.
relation_to_candidate_a: Strong static layer-removal background but not Candidate A's temporal or matched-control result.

title: SLEB: Streamlining LLMs through Redundancy Verification and Elimination of Transformer Blocks
authors: Jiwon Song; Kyungseok Kim; Jaehoon Cho; Sangwook Kim; Jung-Woo Shin; Joonho Moon
abstract: Calibration-based block elimination selects redundant transformer blocks for efficient LLM inference.
main_claim: Output-grounded calibration can guide block removal.
relation_to_candidate_a: Static pruning baseline; no training dynamics or top-1-family matching.

title: BlockPruner: Fine-grained Pruning for Large Language Models
authors: Lei Zhong; Fei Wan; Ruijun Chen; Xiaojun Quan; Liang Li
abstract: MHA and MLP sub-block pruning gives finer-grained structural compression than whole-layer deletion.
main_claim: Sub-layer granularity improves pruning trade-offs.
relation_to_candidate_a: Adjacent structural-pruning work only.

title: As Easy as PIE: Understanding When Pruning Causes Language Models to Disagree
authors: Pietro Tropeano; Maria Maistro; Tuukka Ruotsalo; Christina Lioma
abstract: Pruning disproportionately changes predictions on a stable subset of difficult and influential examples.
main_claim: Aggregate accuracy hides concentrated prediction instability after pruning.
relation_to_candidate_a: Conceptually close to token-level agreement but not layer-bypass trajectories.

title: Reducing Transformer Depth on Demand with Structured Dropout
authors: Angela Fan; Edouard Grave; Armand Joulin
abstract: LayerDrop trains one transformer to support multiple inference depths.
intervention_type: Training-time layer dropout and inference removal
main_claim: Explicit training can make depth removal robust.
relation_to_candidate_a: Background showing deletion robustness can be training-induced by objective; Candidate models were not LayerDrop-trained.

title: Accelerating Training of Transformer-Based Language Models with Progressive Layer Dropping
authors: Xiaodong Zhang; Houxiang He
abstract: Progressively increasing layer dropping accelerates transformer training while preserving quality.
main_claim: Layer reliance can be shaped by a dropout schedule.
relation_to_candidate_a: Optimization background, not post-hoc robustness trajectory.

title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
authors: Stella Biderman et al.
abstract: Pythia releases controlled model scales, checkpoints, and training details for studying learning dynamics.
main_claim: Open checkpoints enable causal and temporal analysis of pretraining.
relation_to_candidate_a: Data/model resource underlying both Candidate A and closest collisions; not a competing finding.

title: Causal Mediation Analysis for Interpreting Neural NLP: The Case of Gender Bias
authors: Jesse Vig; Sebastian Gehrmann; Yonatan Belinkov; Sharon Qian; Daniel Nevo; Yaron Singer; Stuart Shieber
abstract: Causal mediation interventions estimate how internal components mediate behavior.
main_claim: Internal interventions can support targeted causal attribution under explicit assumptions.
relation_to_candidate_a: Mechanistic-intervention boundary context; Candidate A is aggregate robustness, not mediation.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
authors: Kevin Meng; David Bau; Alex Andonian; Yonatan Belinkov
abstract: Causal tracing localizes factual associations and rank-one editing modifies them.
primary_metric: Causal tracing effect and edit efficacy
main_claim: Specific MLP layers mediate factual recall.
relation_to_candidate_a: Intervention methodology background; not robustness or training trajectory.

title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
authors: Fred Zhang; Neel Nanda
abstract: Activation-patching conclusions depend on corruption, metric, and patching choices.
main_claim: Metric and protocol choices materially change intervention conclusions.
relation_to_candidate_a: Supports Candidate A's assay-control motivation; no direct empirical collision.

title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking For? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
authors: Aleksandar Makelov; George Lange; Atticus Geiger; Neel Nanda
abstract: Subspace patching can yield apparently causal directions that do not correspond to the claimed computation.
main_claim: Intervention success alone can be an interpretability illusion.
relation_to_candidate_a: Known-explanation/validity warning; not a layer robustness trajectory.

title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
authors: Atticus Geiger; Hanson Lu; Thomas Icard; Christopher Potts
abstract: Interchange interventions formalize when neural computations implement causal abstractions.
main_claim: Causal abstraction requires structured intervention correspondence.
relation_to_candidate_a: Conceptual boundary for interchange; Candidate A makes no causal-abstraction claim.

title: Agreement-on-the-Line: Predicting the Performance of Neural Networks under Distribution Shift
authors: Hyelin Baek; Yiding Jiang; Aditi Raghunathan; J. Zico Kolter
abstract: Pairwise model agreement can predict out-of-distribution accuracy under certain shifts.
main_claim: Prediction agreement is an established behavioral statistic with limits.
relation_to_candidate_a: Conceptually related agreement metric; not token-level or perturbation trajectory.

title: On the Distance Between Two Neural Networks and the Stability of Learning
authors: Jeremy Bernstein; Arash Vahdat; Yisong Yue; Ming-Yu Liu
abstract: Deep relative trust bounds functional and gradient change using layerwise relative parameter perturbations.
main_claim: Euclidean parameter distance alone misses deep compositional perturbation structure.
relation_to_candidate_a: Known theoretical reason raw norm need not determine functional damage.

title: Sparsifying Networks by Traversing Geodesics
authors: Nikhil Raghavan; Matt Thomson
abstract: A function-space metric tensor maps weight perturbations to behavioral changes for pruning paths.
main_claim: Parameter perturbations should be evaluated through induced function geometry.
relation_to_candidate_a: Known explanation for parameter/function mismatch; no LM trajectory.

title: APEX: Probing Neural Networks via Activation Perturbation
authors: Tao Ren; Xiaoyu Luo; Qiongxiu Li
abstract: Gaussian activation perturbations reveal output-distribution transitions and training biases.
main_claim: Activation robustness is layer- and model-dependent.
relation_to_candidate_a: Close activation-noise measurement context; no Pythia checkpoint family matching.

title: Rethinking Pruning Large Language Models: Benefits and Pitfalls of Reconstruction Error Minimization
authors: Sungho Shin et al.
abstract: Local reconstruction objectives can misalign with end-to-end language-model quality during pruning.
main_claim: Local perturbation proxies need not predict functional outcomes.
relation_to_candidate_a: Supports output-grounded controls; not temporal Candidate A.

title: Investigating Layer Importance in Large Language Models
authors: Aditya Zhang et al.
abstract: Layer ablations reveal nonuniform importance and interactions in LLMs.
main_claim: Some layers are disproportionately important and layer effects interact.
relation_to_candidate_a: Static layer-importance context; no trajectory/matching.

title: Evolving Subnetwork Training for Large Language Models
authors: Anonymous/venue metadata verified on PMLR record
abstract: Training with evolving subnetworks reduces compute while retaining final quality.
main_claim: Redundancy can be exploited during training with controlled budgets.
relation_to_candidate_a: Background on trained robustness, not post-hoc intervention response.

title: The Junk DNA Hypothesis: Pruning Small Pre-Trained Weights Irreversibly and Monotonically Impairs Difficult Downstream Tasks
authors: Zihang Yin et al.
abstract: Magnitude pruning can selectively impair difficult tasks even when aggregate effects look small.
main_claim: Small weights can be functionally important and mean metrics can hide selective damage.
relation_to_candidate_a: General perturbation-importance warning; no checkpoint trajectory.

title: Analyzing Redundancy in Pretrained Transformer Models
authors: Fahim Dalvi; Hassan Sajjad; Nadir Durrani; Yonatan Belinkov
abstract: Representation and neuron analyses show substantial redundancy in pretrained transformers.
main_claim: Pretrained transformers contain redundant representations and units.
relation_to_candidate_a: Foundational static redundancy context.
